q1_issues.issue: 'maturity' is an invented scale — the text says only 'two-year note' and states no dimension word, so no words in the sentence put that symbol there.

(Fraction 5 32) sits in a Measure magnitude slot, but Fraction is defined only as a ProportionOf level and a Measure magnitude must be a native number; the unit 'point' is likewise invented, the text saying only '5/32'.
The atom states the falling event's price AS 5/32 rather than the size of the change, so a delta is recorded as an absolute value.

Two contradictory Measure atoms put the same yield symbol at both 1.16 percent (statement 10) and 1.23 percent with no time index, and the take event's stated endpoints are lost — no Source for 'from 1.16 percent' and no Goal for 'to 1.23 percent'.
'late on Monday' is attached as the Time of the fall (and again to the take at statement 16), although it modifies the 1.16 percent level the yield stood at; 'late' is dropped entirely.

q2_gaps: an attributive measure modifier with no stated dimension ('the two-year note') — Measures & units supplies a scale only from a stated gradable adjective or a measure verb/noun
the magnitude of a CHANGE ('fell 5/32'; 'taking its yield to 1.23 percent from 1.16 percent') — no licensed form for a delta, nor for one entity's value moving between two time-indexed levels
a free participial adjunct of result (', taking its yield to ...') — the participle rules cover post-modifiers on nouns, not a clause-level adjunct with the matrix clause as its implicit subject
notes: Every head used is a defined operator; the defects sit in the argument slots (invented scale and unit, Fraction in a magnitude slot) and in asserting two mutually exclusive yields of one symbol. The ticker treated as a proper noun with its adjacent 'note' kind atom, and Patient on the intransitive change-of-state 'fell', are both correct.
